  • Vinaya – bhante Maggavihāri
    • Entrance to Khandhaka Vinaya (Part I) #edited
      • introduction
        • two levels of vinaya
          • vinaya (pārājikapāḷi and pācittiyapāḷi)
            • vinayo (m.) [vi + √nī + *a]→discipline; training; lit. leading; 2: monastic law; code of monastic disciplinary rules; 3: removal; dispelling; 4: settlement; judgement; verdict #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
            • vinayati √nī→pr. (+acc) removes; dispels #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
          • abhivinaya (khandhaka and parivāra)
        • when we study vinaya we have the ability to purify our own sīla and that of others
      • Pabbajjā: Ordination
        • background
          • During the early period ordination (pabbajjā) and higher ordination (upasampadā) were performed concurrently. Later on the Buddha declared them as two separate disciplinary acts.
          • Two types of monk status
            • sāmaṇera/ī
            • upasampadā
            • (for women there is also sikkhamāna in between sāmaṇerī and bhikkhunī)
        • sāmaṇera pabbajjā (ordination of novices)
          • how is the candidate for ordination called?→pabbajjāpekkha
          • 3 main sections and subsections of pabbajjā
            • 1. bhaṇḍukamma / kesacchedana (shaving act)
              • informing the saṅgha
              • shaving
              • bathing
              • requesting ordination
            • 2. kāsāvacchādana (wearing the robes)
              • giving the robes to the teacher
              • requesting the robes back
              • wearing the robes
            • 3. saraṇadāna (undertaking refuge)
              • requesting refuge and precepts
              • giving refuge and precepts
            • after ordination: upajjhāyaggāha
            • note: all 3 can be called pabbajjā
          • who can perform each step of the process of pabbajjā?
            • informing the saṅgha: upasampanna or sāmaṇera following orders
            • bhaṇḍukamma / kesacchedana: anyone, even the candidate himself but it is something that better be performed by the upasampanna
            • kāsāvacchādana / handing robes to the pabbajjāpekkha: the preceptor himself or someone else (bhikkhu, sāmaṇera or layperson) under the order of the preceptor (should not be worn by oneself)
              • Bhikkhunā hi sahatthena vā āṇattiyā vā dinnameva kāsāvaṃ vaṭṭati, adinnaṃ na vaṭṭati (mhv-a)
            • saraṇadāna: qualified upa (10 vassa, etc. for ācariya / upajjhāya) or byatta paṭibala upa (knows the procedure well and can recite correctly) acting under his orders
              • srtdpn: saraṇadāna should be done by the preceptor or teacher
                • pabbājetī”ti vuccati...tasmā etaṃ pabbājehīti kesacchedanaṃ kāsāyacchādanañca sandhāya vuttaṃ.
              • vmtvndn: suggests that the 3 steps can be done by a byatta patibala upa
              • jnk: byatta paṭibala is ok when following orders of the upajjhāya
              • mhv-a: athassa upajjhāyena vā ācariyena vā “Buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmī”tiādinā nayena saraṇāni dātabbāni yathāvuttapaṭipāṭiyāva na uppaṭipāṭiyā.
              • pabbajjācariya and upajjhāya can be the same upa or not
          • compulsory factors for pabbajjā to be valid
            • wearing robes having accepted them from the teacher (indirectly from a monk or sāmaṇera is also valid)
            • proper recitation of refuge by both the preceptor and the candidate (most basic factor)
              • If the robes are given from the candidate to the preceptor indirectly is it valid?→yes, it is valid
          • bhaṇḍukamma
            • If upasampannā is involved in the bhaṇḍukamma it must be informed to the saṅgha, otherwise it is a {{44100013691564177::dkṭ }}offense. If a sāmaṇera or layperson does it it is not necessary but better to do so. The ideal is for upasampannas to perform bhaṇḍukamma.
              • is there a collective term for sāmaṇeras and sāmaṇerīs? can anupasampanna be used? #q🙋🏼‍♂
              • what about sikkhāmānas? how is their ordination process and so on? #q🙋🏼‍♂
              • Shouldn't the Saṅgha be informed regardless of who is performing the bhaṇḍukamma?→It is not necessary but better to do so since the purpose of the rule is that the residents come to know of a candidate being ordained. In most cases the upasampannas are involved in the kamma and the Saṅgha is informed
            • Informing the Saṅgha: 4 ways:
              • by gathering all the bhikkhus in the vihāra
              • by going to where each bhikkhu stays
              • by a messenger (another bhikkhu or sāmaṇera)
              • by informing only those that are within a baddha sīmā
              • Pāḷi for informing the saṅgha of the shaving: {{7929879004433074::"Saṅghaṃ bhante, imassa dārakassa bhaṇḍukammaṃ āpucchāmi"}}
              • If the candidate is shaven without prior informing of the saṅgha it is a {{2659138699757342::dkṭ offense}}
                • dkṭ offense for whom? upajjhāya certainly (or is it for the pabbajjācariya?) I heard all bhikkhus in the vihāra, is it true? #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • Shaving
              • hair longer than {{2719609929156175::two finger breadths}} must be shaved. It can be done by {{2719609929156175::a bhikkhu, sāmaṇera or lay person (including the candidate himself, but it is something that better be undertaken by the bhikkhus)}}
              • It is a custom to teach the {{43903632923161284::tacapañcaka}} kammaṭṭhāna {{43903632923161284::(kesā, lomā, nakhā, dantā, taco)}} during the procedure. Ven. {{43903632923161284::Sīvali}} attained arahatship by reflecting on tacapañcaka during his bhaṇḍukamma
              • khuragga↔shaving house #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • Is ordination still valid if the bhaṇḍukamma is not done?→yes
              • if the candidate has hair longer than 2 finger-breadths is ordination valid?→it is valid
            • Bathing
              • one must become clean to remove the lay odor
              • A custom practiced in some monasteries: rubbing {{3190994071672111::filtered clay}} on the body, washing it off, applying {{3190994071672111::turmeric}} and washing it off again
              • If the person getting ordained is unable to bathe the teacher should bathe and clean the expectant of ordination with kindness like a father
              • pabbajjāpekkha should be dressed in clean clothes and taken to the place of ordination
            • Requesting Ordination
              • The candidate should pay respect to the parents and saṅgha; with robes in hand, crouch in front of the preceptor-teacher, worship him and request ordination as follows: Pāḷi for requesting ordination with robes in hand: {{579926689894757::Okāsa, ahaṃ bhante, pabbajjaṃ yācāmi. (3x)}}
          • kāsāvacchādana (Wearing the robes)
            • Is ordination valid if refuge is taken without wearing robes?→no, it is a basic factor for pabbajjā to be valid
            • Giving the robes (requesting the teacher to accept the robes)
              • Pāḷi for requesting the robes to be accepted: {{7762792260373894::"(Sakalavaṭṭa-) / Sabba-dukkha-nissaraṇa-nibbāna (/nibbānassa)-sacchikaraṇatthāya imaṃ kāsāvaṃ gahetvā pabbājetha maṃ bhante, anukampaṃ upādāya (3x)}}
              • The robes from the candidate’s hands should be given to the preceptor
                • can pabbajjā be done in another language?→All except the saraṇadāna can be done in another language but it is traditionally done in pāḷi #important
            • Asking for the robes (requesting the teacher to give the robes)
              • Pāḷi for requesting the robes from the teacher: {{8312774372945098::"(Sakalavaṭṭa-) / Sabba-dukkha-nissaraṇa-nibbāna-(/nibbānassa) sacchikaraṇatthāya }}{{8312774372945098::etaṃ}}{{8312774372945098:: kāsāvaṃ }}{{8312774372945098::datvā }}{{8312774372945098::pabbājetha maṃ bhante, anukampaṃ upādāya (3x) }}
              • Robes should be handed back to the candidate by the teacher or by another bhikkhu or sāmaṇera on his order.
            • Wearing the robes
              • After having done cīvarapaccavekkhaṇa the candidate should wear the robes. The teacher or another bhikkhu or sāmaṇera on his order should assist him.
              • Obtaining the robes from the preceptor (indirectly by a bhikkhu or sāmaṇera under the orders of the teacher is also valid) is a compulsory matter in ordination.
              • If robes were worn before the ordination what should be done?→ordination should be done only after removing those robes and handing them over again to the candidate by monks.
          • saraṇadāna (Giving refuge)
            • (Pāḷi) requesting saraṇa and precepts by the pabbajjāpekkha: "Okāsa, ahaṃ bhante, tisaraṇena saddhiṃ / saha pabbajjā(dasa)sīlaṃ dhammaṃ yācāmi. Anuggahaṃ katvā sīlaṃ detha me bhante (3x)
            • (Pāḷi) answer by the teacher: "Yamahaṃ vadāmi taṃ vadehi / vadetha"
            • (Pāḷi) saraṇadāna by the teacher and student alternatively: "Buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi...Dutiyampi...Tatiyampi..."
            • (Pāḷi) conclusion of the saraṇa (optional I think): "Tisaraṇagamanaṁ paripuṇṇaṁ"
            • (Pāḷi) undertaking precepts (optional but usually done): "Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī...adinnādānā...abrahmacariyā...musāvādā...surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā...vikālabhojanā...naccagītavāditavisūkadassanā...mālāgandhavilepanadhāraṇavibhūsanaṭṭhānā...uccāsayanamahāsayanā...jātarūparajatapaṭiggahaṇā..."
            • What are the two methods of pronunciation?→Niggahītanta (ending with ‘ṃ’ and connecting words: Buddhaṁ-saraṇaṁ-gacchāmi...) and the Makāranta (ending with ‘m’ - not connecting words: Buddham saraṇam gacchāmi...). It is better to do so in both ways.
            • Is saraṇadāna valid in any language and method of recitation?→For laity yes, since cetanā is the main factor. For sāmaṇeras it must be in pāḷi with proper pronunciation.
            • in samanera ordination: if the upajjhāya is pārājika it is (valid/not valid?) {{07620867115899621::still valid}}. If the pabbajjācariya is pārājika it is (valid/not valid?){{07620867115899621::not valid}}.
            • upajjhāya (preceptor) and pabbajjācariya (saraṇadāna) can also be the same bhikkhu.
            • "yo saraṇam deti yo pabbajjācariyo"
            • can bhikkhus give saraṇadāna to sāmaṇerīs→no
          • sāmaṇera sīla
            • 10 liṅganāsana (10 pārājikā for sāmaṇera)
            • 10 daṇḍakammanāsana (entails punishment)
            • 75 sekhiyā
            • 14 duties
            • Total of sāmaṇera precepts: in brief 10, in detail 109
        • 10 sikkhāpada (10 precepts)
          • 1st pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṁ samādiyāmi
            • 5 sambhāra (factors): #important
              • pāṇo (object is a living being)
              • pāṇasaññī (perception of a living being)
              • vadhakacittaṁ (intention to kill)
              • upakkamo (means to kill)
              • tena jīvitanāso / tena maraṇaṁ (by that (effort) that life is destroyed) #q🙋🏼‍♂
              • Stanza: "Pāṇo have pāṇasaññī, vadhakacittamupakkamo, tena jīvitanāso ca, aṅgā pañca vadhassime."
            • If the being dies even after several years from a blow struck with the intention to kill the precept will be broken with effect from {{6497627095276219::the very instant of striking}}{{6497627095276219::.}}
          • 2nd adinnādānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṁ samādiyāmi
            • 5 sambhāra #important
              • 1. parapariggahitaṃ (An object that belongs to another human)
              • 2. parapariggahitasaññitā (perceiving the object as belonging to another human)
              • 3. theyyacittaṃ (intention to steal it)
              • 4. upakkamo (attempt on stealing it)
              • 5. tena haraṇaṃ (taking the object by that attempt)
            • 4 exceptions to stealing: #important
              • sakasaññā (as belonging to oneself)
              • paṁsukūlasaññā (one perceives the object as discarded, ownerless)
              • vissāsaggāhī (taking on trust)
              • tāvakālikasaññā (taking temporarily)
            • There is no freedom to take other's properties because a loss has been cause to you. If a thief steals one's property, forcing it to be returned will break the precept but {{3977863993961184::if one still perceives the property as belonging to oneself}} one may get it back
          • 3rd abrahmacariyā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṁ samādiyāmi
            • 2 sambhāra: #q🙋🏼‍♂ #important
              • tassa pana abrahmacariyassa dve sambhārā: sevetukāmatācittaṃ (intention of having sex)
              • maggenamaggapaṭipatti (a penis enters one of the maggas)
              • obs: be careful here, these factors are different from the kāmesumicchācāra (akusalakammapatha) which are 4 (agamanīyavatthu, tasmiṁ sevanacittaṁ, sevanappayogo, maggenamaggapaṭipattiadhivāsanaṁ)
            • payoga: only {{6725673053949144::sāhatthika}}
            • does masturbation break the precept?→No, but it makes the brahmacariya impure and is a daṇḍakamma vatthu
          • 4th musāvādā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṁ samādiyāmi
            • 4 sambhāra: #important
              • atathaṃ vatthu (not the truth)
              • visaṃvādanacittaṃ (intention of deceiving)
              • tajjo vāyāmo (effort at deceiving)
              • parassa tadatthavijānanaṃ (the listener understands the conveyed meaning)
                • Ven. Janakābhivaṁsa (Myanmar) is of the opinion that if the listener understands but is not deceived the precept is broken but in the case of the akusalakammapatha it is not complete
            • what if a lie is uttered for fun? Is the precept broken?→precept is broken
            • what if a lie is uttered in another language and the listener does not understand?→precept is not broken
          • 5th surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṁ samādiyāmi
            • 4 aṅga: #important
              • majjabhāvo (being an intoxicant which causes mada and pamāda)
                • Here mada is {{2591829586026124::conceit associated with powerful delusion }}and pamāda {{2591829586026124::is living with attachment to five sensual pleasures committing unwholesome actions (heedlessness)}}
                • davo √dū (m.)↔fun; joke; play; sport; pleasure
                • mado (m.) √mad↔excess; pleasure; indulgence; vanity; pride; conceit; poisoning; lit. intoxication
              • pātukamyatācittaṃ (intention to take it knowing it is an intoxicant)
              • tajjo vāyāmo (effort at taking it)
              • ajjhoharaṇaṃ (the intoxicant enters the body)
              • obs: here, for sāmaṇeras, only if done while knowing the substance is an intoxicant it breaks the precept but for bhikkhus it would be an offense even if the substance is taken unknowingly (surāmerayapāne pācittiyaṁ)
            • taking medicines which contain alcohol breaks the precept? {{3013387843466824::if it smells or tastes of alcohol the precept will be broken otherwise not}}
            • what if a small amount of alcohol is taken which is not enough to cause intoxication? Is the precept broken?→even taking a single drop breaks the precept
              • if even a single drop breaks the precept how can medicines which contain alcohol in small doses not break it? #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • is tobacco an intoxicant?→its effects are limited to a faintish feeling of the body and does not cause mada or pamāda therefore it does not break the precept #q🙋🏼‍♂
          • 6th vikālabhojanā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṁ samādiyāmi
            • 4 sambhāra #important
              • being vikāla
              • being a yāvakālika
              • knowing it is yāvakālika (for sāmaṇeras)
              • swallowing it
            • 4 types of edibles #important
              • yāvakālika: to be taken only from dawn to midday
              • yāmakālika: edibles which can be taken from midday to dawn
              • sattāhakālika: seven days medicine
              • yāvajīvika: lifetime medicine
            • The morning can be divided into two periods:
              • purebhatta: before the meal
              • pacchābhatta: after the meal but before midday
            • what is dawn and when does it happen according to vinaya?→dawn is the break of the day, the first appearance of light in the morning before sunrise. It occurs when a reddish light is seen in the eastern sky before sunrise
            • when does the day begin according to vinaya?→the day begins at dawn
            • when is midday?→midday is when the sun is half way through its course starting in the eastern horizon and ending in the western. It is when it reaches its highest point in the sky. It can be calculated by dividing the total amount of time from sunrise to sunset and adding that amount to the time of sunrise.
            • special medicines
              • bhisakka saṁyoga: medicine mix which is allowed (mahāvagga)
                • flour in jaggery for consistency is allowed
                • bhisakko (m.)↔doctor, physician, healer
              • loṇasovīraka: medicinal tonic with meat which is allowed
          • 7th naccagītavāditavisukkadassanā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṁ samādiyāmi
            • 2 types of recitation/songs #important
              • {{3445646153785069::Gītupasaṁhita dhamma }}(Dhamma recited in a musical way as a song): for a monk to do so (breaks/does not break the precept?) {{3445646153785069::breaks the precept.}} {{3445646153785069::Dhammupasaṁhita gīta}}{{3445646153785069:: }}(Song sung with Dhamma verses): for a monk to do so (breaks/does not break the precept?){{3445646153785069::breaks the precept but listening to it is allowable}}
                • If there are instruments as well or only voice? #q🙋🏼‍♂
                • upasaṃhita √dhā↔1: (adj.) (+instr) connected (with); concerning; to do (with); 2: (pp.) (mentally) connected, associated
                • It is not allowed to drag the sounds for {{4265972602842125::3 or more mattā (measure)}}
                  • 1 mattā (a), 2 mattā (ā), 3 mattā (āa) not allowed
                    • mattā (f.)
                      • [√mā + ta]
                        • (+gen) measure (of); measurement; quantity; degree (of);
                        • adj. mere; simple; the fact of; by virtue of ;
                        • adj. so much; some; enough (of); sufficient;
                      • [√mad + ta]
                        • pp. intoxicated; drunk; besotted;
                        • adj. (of an elephant) in rut; sexually inflamed; on heat; lit. intoxicated;

            • vehicles
              • Riding on animals or vehicles that are dragged
                • People criticized bhikkhus who were riding on animals so the Buddha laid down a training rule forbidding it. The reason is {{6149320496832313::it exhaust the animal as a type of mild torture.}} This rule included vehicles dragged by human beings. A bhikkhu is allowed to use them only {{6149320496832313::when sick}} except when dragged by females which is not allowed. For the purpose of preaching dhamma it is {{6149320496832313::not allowed either}} .
              • Modern vehicles
                • Riding on a car/bus with a female driver is allowed or not?→Since most modern vehicles are not dragged these rules do not apply to them therefore riding on a car with a female driver cannot be said to be an offense but some traditions do not do that.
              • Ships and boats
                • The rules are more lenient when it comes to ships and boats. Are they allowed or not?→They are allowed even when paddled/dragged by animals or people including women but it is not allowed for the monks to paddle
              • Other vehicles
                • Being taken on a cart dragged by a human being is allowed or not?→Because it is close to the dragging of an animal it is better to avoid it even though a clear cut answer cannot be given.
          • 10th jātarūparajatapaṭiggahaṇā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṁ samādiyāmi
            • jātarūpa (nt.)↔gold, lit. genuine matter; like the color of the Buddha #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
            • Why money is not allowed for monks?
              • money is very desirable
              • "if money was allowed for bhikkhus all sense pleasures would be allowed."
              • The Buddha allows bhikkhus to even go to the extent of collecting grains, bread, and so on for travelling, but in no instance money is allowed.
              • When bhikkhus have needs the laity may not be able to provide them and when the laity is able to provide them the bhikkhus may not have any needs therefore the Buddha allowed proper ways through which bhikkhus can receive allowable things.
            • No rules are broken for the arising of a thought
              • The purpose of vinaya is for restraining and purifying physical and verbal behavior and meditation is for the purpose of purifying mental behavior
              • Rules which are very close to being broken just by mind:
                • The 1st parajika according to one commentator's opinion. The tradition explains it as a bodily action but not with much success.
                • This sikkhāpada: if when offered money a bhikkhu mentally consents to receiving it and does not reject it it is an offense.
            • If money is accepted by upasampanna
              • The Buddha allowed a way for accepted money to be used for the benefit of the saṅgha righteously. The offender should relinquish the money according to the proper procedure in the presence of the saṅgha (saṅghamajjhe) and the laity can use it for offering allowable things.
              • Kammavācā for the forfeiture of money accepted by an upasampanna. To be done among the saṅgha (incomplete): {{6286658282309467::"Ahaṁ, bhante, rūpiyaṁ paṭiggahesiṁ. Idaṁ me nissaggiyaṁ. Imāhaṁ saṅghassa nissajjāmi."}}{{6286658282309467:: }}
              • How should properties coming from previously accepted money be treated? (the offender accepted money, relinquished it properly and the laity used it for offering allowable things)
                • the offender cannot use the requisites arranged from that money he accepted but other sahadhammikas can. Even though those things cannot be shared as personal properties.
              • How should properties bought by bhikkhus be treated?
                • Things that have been bought by the offenders cannot be used by any of the sahadhammikas ever and this cannot be corrected
                • If the offender builds a personal kuti with accepted money and then disrobes, maybe it is ok, we will discuss later.
            • Relinquishing the accepted money without the proper procedure
              • It is allowable to relinquish the money to a layperson but it is suggested to do so {{03397271296447202::to someone beyond the circle of kappiyakārakas to avoid expecting an invitation from the kappiyas}}. It is better to do the proper procedure because {{03397271296447202::the money can be used for the sake of the saṅgha as intended by the Buddha.}}
            • When someone offers gold/money and keeps it in front of a monk what should be done?→the monk must reject it. If not rejected and accepted in the mind by remaining silent the precept is broken #important
              • If it is not rejected but not accepted in the mind the precept is not broken. (TBC) #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • Does touching money without accepting it breaks the precept or not?→it will not break the precept but as money is considered an untouchable item it is good for sāmaṇeras to not even touch money. In the case of picking up and holding gold/money for safekeeping within the monastery intending on returning it to the owner it is allowed. #important
            • How should a sāmaṇera relinquish money?→There is no protocol established. They can relinquish it to a lay person who better be outside of the close circle of kappiyakārakas. #important
            • How to inform a layperson of the presence of gold/money?→It is allowable to inform the laity of the presence of some gold/money by saying: "imaṁ jānāhi" without asking for anything. The layperson can do with it as it pleases and if the layperson makes an invitation monks can ask for allowable things.
            • kappiya↔allowable (s.w. k)
            • Can the money accepted by a sāmaṇera be used by the saṅgha?→No, money cannot be used by any sahadhammikas. It should be relinquished and the sāmaṇera given daṇḍakamma.
            • if money is accepted by asahadhammikas who are 10 preceptors (including sayalays) can the requisites coming from that money be accepted?→Yes. (bh. Mgvhr "but it is not ethical") #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • Pañcasahadhammika (five co-religionists) #important
              • Bhikkhu
              • Bhikkhunī
              • Sikkhamānā
              • Sāmaṇera
              • Sāmaṇerī
            • Asahadhammika↔not one of the 5 coreligionists.
        • nissaya (dependence upon preceptor)
          • Pāḷi formulas:
            • Pāḷi: "evañca pana, bhikkhave, upajjhāyo gahetabbo –
              • ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘upajjhāyo me, bhante, hohi, upajjhāyo me, bhante, hohi, upajjhāyo me, bhante, hohī’ti. sāhūti vā lahūti vā opāyikanti vā patirūpanti vā pāsādikena sampādehīti vā kāyena viññāpeti, vācāya viññāpeti, kāyena vācāya viññāpeti, gahito hoti upajjhāyo, na kāyena viññāpeti, na vācāya viññāpeti, na kāyena vācāya viññāpeti, na gahito hoti upajjhāyo."
            • Pāḷi for requesting dependence from the upajjhāya #important
              • "Upajjhāyo me bhante hohi" (3x) ⇒ Answer: sāhū / lahū / opāyikaṁ / patirūpaṁ / pāsādikena sampādehi The upajjhāya may also answer in another language (such as saying "ok") or with bodily gestures as well. (kāyena / vācāya viññāpeti)

                • pāsādika √sad (vis.)↔pleasing; inspiring confidence; lit. causing to settle
            • How many times the request for dependence from the upajjhāya is done?―only once and it cannot be revoked or lost unless one falls into pārājika or disrobes.
              • Sāmaṇeras in SL usually request dependence on upajjhāya every time they undertake saraṇagamana. They do so even to other teachers who are not the original upajjhāya. That is done because if any of the liṅganāsana factors were broken they lost their novicehood and should reordain but this practice may not be correct.
              • Sāmaṇeras who are pārājika are not like a layman. They still have the samaṇa status. #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • requesting nissaya from the ācariya
              • request: "ācariyo me bhante (/āvuso) hohi, āyasmato nissāya vacchāmi" Answer (verbal / bodily): "sāhū / lahū / opāyikaṁ / patirūpaṁ / pāsādikena sampādehi" (any language)

          • why does the Buddha want monks to take dependence on a preceptor/teacher?
            • apart from one's personal practice as a monk one must be able to represent the teaching properly and be able to maintain the lineage for the benefit of others. Therefore even arahat monks must learn under a teacher for 5 years accordingly.
            • Maghadevasutta (MN) summary - custom established by the bodhisatta of renouncing kingship after the hair was ripe. Later as a brahma he looked down and saw one king did not follow the custom and it was lost. He then took birth as a human and re-established the custom. "Don't be the last monks in the sāsana. I will not come back to re-establish the lineage of monks."
            • Even the Buddha Himself lived dependent on the Dhamma He realized
            • Well written books do not substitute a teacher. For the laity it may be enough for dhamma practice but not for ordained people because there are many practical things that are not in the books, because one needs corrections, because doubts may arise, because one needs examples, etc...

        • nāsana
          • 3 types of nāsana
            • saṁvāsanāsana (excommunication)
              • This nāsana is related to which vinayakamma?→ukkhepanīyakamma (excommunication) #important
              • Ukkhepanīyakamma is only done against bhikkhus or bhikkhunīs who
                • hold wrong views
                  • Bh. Raṭṭha (tbc) held the wrong view that sense pleasures were not a hindrance for monks because Noble lay disciples who had attained the first and second paths could have sex. What he missed was the status of a monk.
                    • status of a monk is not just a concept. To be discussed. #q🙋🏼‍♂
                • repeatedly commit heavy offenses
                • or do not accept admonishment
              • The bhikkhu / bhikkhunī who has received ukkhepanīyakamma is called {{4045422133273837::ukkhittaka.}}
              • Unless an upasampanna has {{17304528318304913::committed a pārājika}} he/she cannot be disrobed but in the case of a sāmaṇera it can be done. (There is the case of one bhikkhunī who was expelled by the Buddha apparently without investigation because the Buddha knew she had already {{17304528318304913::committed a pārājika offense}})
              • Samanubhāsanakamma: preliminary stages before ukkhepanīyakamma is done
              • A bhikkunī who associates ukkhittaka bhikkhus are given samanubhāsanakamma and may end up pārājika (7th prjk - ukkhittānuvattaka).
              • After the ukkhittaka bhikkhu corrects himself and the saṅgha is pleased with him another kamma is done to reinstate him as part of the saṅgha.
              • Pabbajanīyakamma: done against those who corrupt families
                • 500 monks disciples of Bh Sāriputta and Moggallāna were staying at Kitagiri (tbc) city and were corrupting families by giving gifts, riding animals, pleasing the laity, sleeping with women (but not having sex), etc. #tbc🕵
                • 2 liṅgas of a monk
                  • shaven head
                  • robe of patches
                • Pabbajanīyakamma cannot be done against more than {{9384645983898565::3}} bhikkhus at the same time because it would be like a schism.
                • Fun fact: Bh. Sāriputta was the upajjhāya of the chabbagiya bhikkhus as well as some of the bhikkhus who were staying in Kitagiri. This is why the Buddha sent the 2 chief disciples to deal with them.
                • After the kamma was done to those bhikkhus some disrobed. When the Buddha was informed of it He was displeased and asked: "how could they disrobe? The punishment given to them is for the purpose of correcting their conduct not for causing them to suffer."
                • Punishment is not to hurt but to rectify. The sāsana is based on karuṇā.
            • liṅganāsana (disrobing)
              • related to which offenses? {{1564632381327269::pārājikā}}
              • it can be done against {{7176309282282756::all sahadhammikas}}
              • If the sāmaṇera falls into pārājika, he should be {{4313049143775356::disrobed and sent away}} but if he is ready for {{4313049143775356::āyati saṁvara (future restraint)}} , he can be given ordination again.
                • āyati saṁvara↔future discipline/restraint
              • sāmaṇera who is pārājika technically would lose seniority. Nowadays sāmaṇeras do not pay respect to each other and line up according to age. There are different practices on this point.
              • A bhikkhu or a sāmaṇera who is pārājika and is ready for future restraint can be given the status of a {{753242884901824::sāmaṇera}}. A bhikkhunī, sikkhamāna or sāmaṇerī can be given the status of a {{753242884901824::sāmaṇerī}}. The bhikkhu and bhikkhunī cannot obtain upasampadā again but the sikkhamāna, sāmaṇera and sāmaṇerī can obtain it.

              • related to {{5361908565465956::minor offenses}}

          • 10 liṅganāsanaṅga / dasa pārājika for sāmaṇeras
            • anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dasahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ sāmaṇeraṃ nāsetuṃ. pāṇātipātī hoti, (killer)
            • adinnādāyī hoti, (thief)
            • abrahmacārī hoti, (has sex)
            • musāvādī hoti, (liar)
            • majjapāyī hoti, (consumes intoxicants)
            • buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, (speaks in dispraise of the Buddha denying His qualities such as arahaṁ)
              • Not immediately pārājika. The sāmaṇera should be admonished thrice according to the protocol in the pācittiya rule related to this. The same for the next 3.
            • dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, (speaks in dispraise of the Dhamma...)
            • saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, (...of the Saṅgha)
            • micchādiṭṭhiko hoti, (holds wrong views)
              • Doubting a historical event is not vicikicchā. Vicikicchā is about realities.
            • bhikkhunidūsako hoti (has sex with a bhikkhunī) – anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imehi dasahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ sāmaṇeraṃ nāsetunti.
              • why is bhikkhunīdūsaka separated from abrahmacariya precept?→because if the sāmaṇera break the abrahmacariya precept he is still eligible for ordination but by breaking this one he becomes ineligible.
            • If the sāmanera who was pārājika does not establish himself in discipline and repeatedly commits wrong practices he should be {{019774529032250632::disrobed and sent away after informing the Saṅgha. }}If he comes again after becoming disciplined and requests ordination{{019774529032250632:: he can be ordained after informing the Saṅgha.}}
          • 10 daṇḍakammavatthu (basis for penalizations / punishments)
            • last 5 precepts
              • vikālabhojana (eating outside the proper time)
              • naccagītavāditavisūkadassana (dancing, singing and watching shows)
              • mālagandhavilepanadhāraṇavibhūsanaṭṭhāna (wearing adornments, make up, etc)
              • uccāsayanamahāsayana (using high and luxurious beds and seats)
              • jātarūparajayapaṭiggahaṇa (accepting gold, silver and currencies)
            • "anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa sāmaṇerassa daṇḍakammaṃ kātuṃ.
              • bhikkhūnaṃ alābhāya parisakkati (he attempts to cause loss to the bhikkhus),
              • bhikkhūnaṃ anatthāya parisakkati (he attempts to harm the bhikkhus),
              • bhikkhūnaṃ avāsāya parisakkati (he attempts to evict bhikkhus),
              • bhikkhū akkosati paribhāsati (he insults and abuses bhikkhus),
              • bhikkhū bhikkhūhi bhedeti (he causes dissent among the bhikkhus) – anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imehi pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa sāmaṇerassa daṇḍakammaṃ kātunti.
            • mem aid: 5 last precepts of the 10, alabhāya, anatthāya, avāsāya, akkosati, bhedeti
            • parisakkati↔pr. endeavors, tries
            • paribhāsati↔pr. (+acc) abuses; reviles; insults; badmouths
          • daṇḍakammas (penalizations / punishments)
            • when can sāmaṇeras be penalized / punished?
              • due to committing all offenses apart from the 10 liṅganāsanas (including preliminary steps for certain liṅganāsanas), especially for committing acts prohibited by lokāvajja precepts set for bhikkhus.
                • 2 types of offenses according to 2 reasons they should be avoided #important
                  • lokavajja: acts that are certainly done with an unwholesome mind
                    • what about accepting money? is it lokavajja only for monks?→No, it is paṇṇattivajja. There is no difference between lokavajja/paṇṇattivajja for monks or laity
                  • paṇṇatti / paññatti vajja: should be avoided because it has been said by the Buddha
            • how is the sāmaṇera's morality purified?
              • there is no āpatti-desanā for sāmaṇeras, so their morality can only be purified by undergoing daṇḍakamma.
            • why are penalizations given and with which mindset?
              • They are given to help the offender avoid such misconduct in the future not for hurting or causing distress. It should be done without cruelty out of compassion.
            • allowed daṇḍakammas
              • āvaraṇa (allowed but not used)
                • "Anujānāmi bhikkhave, āvaraṇaṃ kātuṃ”. Not allowing the offender sāmaṇera to{{42473209542298185:: go to the residence of the preceptor and the place assigned to him for residing}}
                  • Gaṇṭhipada and Vimativinodaṇi: only prevention of entry into private residence of the teacher/preceptor and of living in the Saṅgha residence the Sāmaṇera received according to his seniority. Sāratthadīpanī: can be applied whether they are private residences or Saṅghika.
                  • Preventing the sāmaṇera from entering the entire monastery is (allowed/not allowed) {{09659339239728615::not allowed. }}{{09659339239728615::“Na bhikkhave, sabbo saṅghārāmo āvaraṇaṃ kātabbo. Yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkave, yattha vā vasati, yattha vā paṭikkamati, tattha āvaraṇaṃ akātunti”}}{{09659339239728615:: }}
              • what are suitable daṇḍakammas? #important
                • carrying water, firewood or sand to suit the offence of the sāmaṇeras was decided as suitable penalizations in the first council (paṭhamasaṅgāyanā). Assigning works such as sweeping that are useful is allowed.
              • how to mete out punishments in case of multiple offenses?
                • In case of multiple offenses a single punishment for all offences is to be meted out.
            • prohibited daṇḍakammas
              • torturous punishments such as {{9958072900829482::arranging to lie on a heated rock surface, getting to carry stones and timber on the head and sinking under water}}
              • mukhadvārika āhāra āvaraṇa (preventing one from eating)
                • the teachers who do so will be subject to {{0025791420379517316::dkṭ}}{{0025791420379517316::.}}Saying "{{0025791420379517316::You can eat after you have undergone this many punishments}}” is allowed but eating should be allowed irrespective of whether the punishment has been undergone or not.
            • who metes out daṇḍakammas
              • It is {{11660133796036631::the preceptor}} who has the power to mete out āvaraṇa daṇḍakamma. For another upasampanna to do so without his consent is a {{11660133796036631::dkṭ. }}"Na, bhikkhave, upajjhāye anāpucchā āvaraṇaṃ kātabbaṃ. Yo kareyya, āpatti {{11660133796036631::dukkaṭassa}}"
                • Does this apply only to āvaraṇa or to other daṇḍakammas such as sweeping as well? #q🙋🏼‍♂
              • If the preceptor does not punish the sāmaṇera even after a bhikkhu informs him on three occasions of a misconduct what should be done?→the sāmaṇera can be penalized by that bhikkhu
            • high ordination duty
              • It is a duty of the teacher-preceptor to establish the sāmaṇeras that are properly protecting morality in higher ordination (upasampadā) at a suitable time

        • upasampadā sīla (morality of higher ordination)
          • Why is it called adhisīla?→the upasampadā sīla brings all great and invaluable mundane and supramundane benefits; it is the highest among all moralities
          • Why is it called pātimokkha saṁvara sīla?→As the one who protects it is released from suffering in apāya realms and self-reproach it is also called ‘pātimokkha saṃvara sīla'.
          • Total number of upasampadā precepts in detail (adhisīla):
            • It has been shown in the Visuddhimagga that the number of precepts to be protected in upasampadā sīla (morality of higher ordination) is ninety-one billion eight hundred and five million and thirty-six thousand.
            • Vmt-ṭ. I. 44: Nava koṭisahassāni, asītisatakoṭiyo; paññāsasatasahassāni, chattiṃsā ca punāpare. Ete saṃvaravinayā, sambuddhena pakāsitā; peyyālamukhena niddiṭṭhā, sikkhā vinayasaṃvare’ti (91 billions 805 millions 36 thousands)
              • Nava koṭisahassāni: 9.000 x 10.000.000 = 90.000.000.000
              • asītisatakoṭiyo: 180 x 10.000.000 = 1.800.000.000
              • paññāsasatasahassāni: 50 x 100.000 = 5.000.000
              • chattiṃsa (sahassa): 36 x 1000 = 36.000
              • TOTAL: 91.805.036.000

          • 8 types of upasampadās (+1)

            • saraṇagamanūpasampadā (by taking refuge)

            • dūtenūpasampadā (by a messenger)
            • aṭṭhavācikūpasampadā (by 8 kammavācās)
            • ñatticatutthakammūpasampadā (by a motion-and-three-proclamations vinaya kamma)

            • (memory aid: 1st, 3, 3, 10, 3 for bhī (8, dūta, 8), 4)
          • Ehibhikkhūpasampadā
            • only conferred to those who fulfilled 4 conditions:
              • males
              • who had the opportunity to become arahats in the same life
              • and who had past merit (including have offered the basic requisites of a bhikkhu in the past)
              • who have requested ordination
            • How did it happen?→When the expectant of ordination requested ordination, the Tathāgata (after having reflected if the candidate had all conditions fulfilled) stretched the right hand and stated, “Ehi bhikkhu, svākkhāto dhammo, caratha brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāya”. With the completion of stating “Ehi bhikkhu” the ordination and higher ordination of the disciple took place, the lay appearance of the expectant of ordination disappeared, his head hair was shaved and he appeared bearing bowl and robes obtained due to his past merits.
            • Pāḷi: {{6514916227989016::Ehi bhikkhu, svākkhāto dhammo, caratha brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāya}}
            • {{6283163967038432::Ven. Aññākoṇḍañña thera}} was the first recipient of ehi bhikkhu upasampadā #important
          • Saraṇagamanūpasampadā (by taking refuge)
            • Background→after the 1st vassa 60 arahats were sent to spread the dhamma and those looking for ordination were brought to the Buddha. An easier means of ordination became necessary and this type of ordination was established by the Buddha. If the candidate was below 20 he would become a sāmaṇera, if above 20 a bhikkhu.
            • How was this ordination done?→It is the same procedure as for sāmaṇera ordination
            • The first recipient is {{8637803758546094::unknown}}
          • Ovādapaṭiggahaṇūpasampadā (by accepting advice)
            • Background
              • Where? {{023583380453831904::in }}{{023583380453831904::Rājagaha, }}{{023583380453831904::under the }}{{023583380453831904::Bahuputtaka Banyan }}{{023583380453831904::tree}} Who was the recipient? {{023583380453831904::a young man }}{{023583380453831904::Piphali }}{{023583380453831904::who ten became Ven. }}{{023583380453831904::Mahākassapatthera}} How did it happen? {{023583380453831904::he met the Buddha and expressed his disciple status saying: "Satthā me bhante bhagavā sāvakohamasmi" the Tathāgata gave the young man Piphali }}{{023583380453831904::three advices}}{{023583380453831904::. His higher ordination took place merely by the acceptance of these advices. In 7 days he attained Arahatship.}}
            • 3 admonishments the Buddha gave to Mahākassapa:
              • always contemplate the repulsiveness of the body (to avoid lust because he was good looking)
              • listen always very attentively to dhamma (to avoid māna because he was wise)
              • when approaching the saṅgha always approach with respect (to avoid māna because he was from the brahmin clan)
            • only one with {{9827480710779708::the 13 dhutaṅgas}} could wear the robe given by the Buddha to Ven. Mahākassapa
            • Can chief disciples pass away after their respective Buddhas?→no, the 2 chief disciples always pass away before their respective Buddhas
          • Pañhabyākaraṇūpasampadā (by solving questions)
            • Background
              • Where? {{20321542073541154::In }}{{20321542073541154::Sāvatthi}}{{20321542073541154::, at the }}{{20321542073541154::Pubbārāma }}{{20321542073541154::monastery}} Recipient? {{20321542073541154::Sopāka }}{{20321542073541154::Sāmaṇera (arahant)}} How old was he? {{20321542073541154::7 years old}} How did it happen? {{20321542073541154::he was }}{{20321542073541154::walking}}{{20321542073541154:: behind the Tathāgata when He turned towards Sopāka Sāmaṇera and }}{{20321542073541154::while standing}}{{20321542073541154:: asked ten questions about the }}{{20321542073541154::unpleasant perception}}{{20321542073541154:: (asubha saññā) (according to Vinaya; but according to Suttanta it was the kumārapañhāsutta). The Sopāka Sāmaṇera solved them all very well. The Tathāgata pleased by it declared the higher ordination of the Sopāka Sāmaṇera.}}
          • Garudhammapaṭiggahaṇūpasampadā (by accepting 8 cardinal rules)
            • Background
              • When (who?) {{4910045128245992::Pajāpatī Gotamī, the stepmother/aunt of the Tathāgata}} requested higher ordination from the Tathāgata, with the assistence of {{4910045128245992::Ven. Ānanda}}, these 8 cardinal rules were established and her acceptance of them resulted in her ordination.
                • Some scholars think the 8 garudhammas were only for pajāpatī but according to theravāda it is for all bhikkhunīs.
          • Dūtenapaṭiggahaṇūpasampadā (by a messenger)
            • Background
              • The ex-prostitute named {{29550851748546436::Aḍḍhakāsī }}got ordained among the bhikkhuṇīs and was preparing to go to the bhikkhusaṅgha to receive upasampadā when it came to be known that {{29550851748546436::a group of men were waiting to rape her.}} Then the Tathāgata approved the sending of another bhikkhunī as an agent in order to perform the upasampadā. This can be done for others as well.
          • Aṭṭhavācikūpasampadā (by 8 kammavācās)
            • Background
              • Bhī ordination was done first by bhikkhusaṅgha (500 followers of pajāpatī and those who changed sex - these are called {{669864486193027::ekato upasampannā}} but because some ladies were ashamed of answering certain questions to the monks during ordination the Buddha established ordination first under bhikkhunīs and then under bhikkhus (aṭṭhavācika (because 2 times ñatticatuttha)). Until they are ordained by the bhikkhu saṅgha they are not yet bhikkhunīs and they are called {{669864486193027::ekato upasampannā as well}}.
            • two types of ekatoupasampannā
              • aparipuṇṇa - not yet bhikkhunī: candidates of upasampadā who have received it from the bhī saṅgha but not yet from the bhikkhu saṅgha (not yet bhikkhunīs)
              • paripuṇṇa - bhikkhunī: those who received ordination from the bhikkhu saṅgha (the 500 followers of pajāpatī and bhikkhus who have changed sex). They are bhikkhunīs.
          • Ñatticatutthakammūpasampadā (by a motion-and-three-proclamations vinaya kamma)
            • Background
              • First recipient? {{10019711323369762::Ven. Rādha}} Who was responsible? {{10019711323369762::Ven. Sāriputta}} How did it happen? {{10019711323369762::he was taken to the Buddha by the elder }}{{10019711323369762::Sāriputta}}{{10019711323369762:: who inquired about the procedure and the Buddha abolished the saraṇagamanūpasampadā and established ñatticatutthakammūpasampadā. Within majjhimadesa 10 bhikkhus are needed in the assembly, outside of it only 5. This is the upasampadā method used nowadays.}} #important
            • motion ({{5906197904970218::ñatti}}) is done in (which tense) {{5906197904970218::present tense}} and proclamations ({{5906197904970218::anusāvana}}) are done in the (which tense) {{5906197904970218::optative mood}}
          • Of the 8 types of upasampadā {{6685760267249063::4}} were done by the Buddha and {{6685760267249063::4}} by the sāvakas
          • Buddhupajjhāyika↔one who has the Buddha as upajjhāya
          • Buddhācariyaka↔one who has the Buddha as ācariya (27.000+ monks)
        • ñatticatutthakammūpasampadā
          • Where can upasampadā be done?→technically anywhere but all bhikkhus of the area must be present or give chanda therefore upasampadās are always done in sīmās.
            • 2 main types of sīmā
              • baddhasīmā - established by the saṅgha
              • abaddhasīmā - not established by the saṅgha (village, forest or water sīmā)
          • upasampadā in the majjhimadesa must be done with at least {{1095053329942246::10}} bhikkhus. Pāḷi: {{1095053329942246::"anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dasavaggena vā atirekadasavaggena vā gaṇena upasampādetuṁ.}} If performed outside of the majjhimadesa only {{1095053329942246::5}} are needed (with one of them being a vinayadhara). Pāḷi: {{1095053329942246::anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sabbapaccantimesu janapadesu vinayadharapañcamena gaṇena upasampadaṃ.}}
          • Majjhimadesa limits:
            • In brief: To the east (The Great Sal Tree after Gajaṅgala town) To the southeast the river Sallavatī To the south the Setakaṇṇika town To the west the brahmin village of Thūna To the north the Usīraddhaja mountain
            • Pāḷi: tatrime paccantimā janapadā – puratthimāya disāya gajaṅgalaṃ [kajaṅgalaṃ (sī. syā.)] nāma nigamo, tassā parena mahāsālā, tato parā paccantimā janapadā, orato majjhe. Puratthimadakkhiṇāya disāya sallavatī [salalavatī (sī.)] nāma nadī, tato parā paccantimā janapadā, orato majjhe. Dakkhiṇāya disāya setakaṇṇikaṃ nāma nigamo, tato parā paccantimā janapadā, orato majjhe. Pacchimāya disāya thūnaṃ nāma brahmaṇagāmo, tato parā paccantimā janapadā, orato majjhe. Uttarāya disāya usīraddhajo nāma pabbato, tato parā paccantimā janapadā, orato majjhe.
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • mahāsālo (m.)→great sal tree (Shorea robusta)
              • paccanta (vis.) [pati + anta]↔border; frontier; outlying
              • orato (nip.)↔on this side (of), on the nearer side; before
          • expectant of higher ordination is called {{23151188456071647::upasampadāpekkha}}
          • Who established the candidate in higher ordination?→It is not the reciters nor the upajjhāya but the saṅgha
          • ordination procedure #important
            • before the ordination and kammavācā (12 steps)
              • bringing the candidate to the saṅgha in the sīmā
              • (optional) changing names: Nāga for upasampadapekkha and Tissa for upajjhāya by informing all present
              • upajjhāyagahaṇa (taking upajjhāya):
                • Pāḷi by the ācariya: {{7325849600222407::"paṭhamaṃ upajjhaṃ gāhāpetabbo"}}
              • pattacīvaraṁ ācikkhitabbaṁ (mentioning bowl and robes)
                • the bowl and robes should belong to the candidate but in case they are not the ordination is still valid
                • kappabindu is done by an upasampanna
                • pāḷi by the ācariya: {{6087660017095191::"upajjhaṃ gāhāpetvā pattacīvaraṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ – ayaṃ te patto, ayaṃ saṅghāṭi, ayaṃ uttarāsaṅgo, ayaṃ antaravāsako." }}
              • sending the candidate to a side
                • pāḷi by the ācariya: {{2707257938052048::"gaccha, amumhi okāse tiṭṭhāhi"}}
                • he should not turn his back to the saṅgha
              • the upasampadācariya requests the saṅgha permission to advise the candidate on a side
                • pāḷi: na, bhikkhave, asammatena {{34920484753270475::anusāsitabbo. yo anusāseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sammatena anusāsituṃ.}}
                • pāḷi for requesting to advise: "{{046294805778852144::suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato upasampadāpekkho. yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, itthannāmo itthannāmaṃ anusāseyyā"ti}}
              • he advises the candidate on a side about the 13 antarāyikadhammas
                • 13 antarāyikadhammas asked during ordination
                  • anujānāmi, bhikkhave, upasampādentena terasa [tassa (ka.)] antarāyike dhamme pucchituṃ. evañca pana, bhikkhave, pucchitabbo – "santi te evarūpā ābādhā – kuṭṭhaṃ, gaṇḍo, kilāso, soso, apamāro? manussosi? purisosi? bhujissosi? aṇaṇosi? nasi rājabhaṭo? anuññātosi mātāpitūhi? paripuṇṇavīsativassosi? paripuṇṇaṃ te pattacīvaraṃ? kiṃnāmosi? konāmo te upajjhāyo"ti?
              • ovādācariya requests the saṅgha permission to bring back the candidate
              • candidate requests ordination
                • ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ kārāpetvā bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vandāpetvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīdāpetvā añjaliṃ paggaṇhāpetvā upasampadaṃ yācāpetabbo – "saṅghaṃ, bhante, upasampadaṃ yācāmi. ullumpatu maṃ, bhante, saṅgho anukampaṃ upādāya. dutiyampi..."
              • ovādācariya requests the saṅgha permission to question the candidate about the 13 antarāyikadhammas
              • he questions the candidate among the Saṅgha
              • kammavācā is recited while the candidate squats
                • What is the ñatti?→is the first kammavācā starting from "suṇātu me bhante saṅgho..." until "esā ñatti"
                • What is the anusāvana?→it is the kammavācā that comes after the ñatti and starts with "suṇātu me..." until "yassa nakkhamati so bhāseyya".
                • What is the difference between each of the 3 anusāvanas?→the sentence "dutiyampi etamatthaṁ vadāmi" appears on the beginning of the second and "tatiampi etamatthaṁ vadāmi" in the beginning of the third.
                • At what moment is the upasampadā effective?→at the very end of the third anusāvana "yassa nakkhamati so bhāseyya"
                • what is the name of the section that comes after the third anusāvana (upasampanno saṅghena...)? #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • after the ordination (3 steps: 4, 4, 4)
              • informing 4 things to the newly ordained about his ordination
                • i. chāyāmetabbā - the time
                • ii. utuppamāṇaṁ ācikkhitabbaṁ - the season
                • iii. divasabhāgo ācikkhitabbo - the section of the day
                  • shouldn't it be the day itself not just the section of the day? #q🙋🏼‍♂
                • iv. saṅgīti ācikkhitabbā - the newly ordained should be informed that if questioned about his ordination particulars he should answer accordingly as he has been informed #q🙋🏼‍♂
              • cattāro nissayā ācikkhitabbā (informing the 4 dependences)
                • 1st nissaya: piṇḍiyālopabhojanaṁ (alms food) additional benefits (allowances): saṅghabhattaṃ, uddesabhattaṃ, nimantanaṃ, salākabhattaṃ, pakkhikaṃ, uposathikaṃ, pāṭipadikaṃ.
                • 2nd nissaya: paṁsukūlacīvaraṁ (discarded robes) additional benefits (allowances): khomaṃ, kappāsikaṃ, koseyyaṃ, kambalaṃ, sāṇaṃ, bhaṅgaṃ.
                • 3rd nissaya: rukkhamūlasenāsanaṃ (the foot of a tree) additional benefits (allowances): vihāro, aḍḍhayogo, pāsādo, hammiyaṃ, guhā
                • 4th nissaya: pūtimuttabhesajjaṃ (putrid urine) additional benefits (allowances): sappi, navanītaṃ, telaṃ, madhu, phāṇita"nti
                • Pāḷi:
                  • piṇḍiyālopabhojanaṃ nissāya pabbajjā. tattha te yāvajīvaṃ ussāho karaṇīyo. atirekalābho – saṅghabhattaṃ, uddesabhattaṃ, nimantanaṃ, salākabhattaṃ, pakkhikaṃ, uposathikaṃ, pāṭipadikaṃ.
                  • paṃsukūlacīvaraṃ nissāya pabbajjā. tattha te yāvajīvaṃ ussāho karaṇīyo. atirekalābho – khomaṃ, kappāsikaṃ, koseyyaṃ, kambalaṃ, sāṇaṃ, bhaṅgaṃ.
                  • rukkhamūlasenāsanaṃ nissāya pabbajjā. tattha te yāvajīvaṃ ussāho karaṇīyo. atirekalābho – vihāro, aḍḍhayogo, pāsādo, hammiyaṃ, guhā.
                  • pūtimuttabhesajjaṃ nissāya pabbajjā. tattha te yāvajīvaṃ ussāho karaṇīyo. atirekalābho – sappi, navanītaṃ, telaṃ, madhu, phāṇita"nti.
              • cattāri akaraṇīyāni ācikkhitabbāni (informing the 4 akaraṇīya)
                • 1st akaraṇīya: not having sex even with an animal
                • 2nd akaraṇīya: not stealing even a blade of grass
                • 3rd akaraṇīya: not killing even an ant
                • 4th akaraṇīya: not expressing exalted states, not even by saying "I delight in an empty dwelling"
                • Pāḷi:
                  • "upasampannena bhikkhunā methuno dhammo na paṭisevitabbo, antamaso tiracchānagatāyapi. yo bhikkhu methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevati, assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo. seyyathāpi nāma puriso sīsacchinno abhabbo tena sarīrabandhanena jīvituṃ, evameva bhikkhu methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevitvā assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo. taṃ te yāvajīvaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ.
                  • "upasampannena bhikkhunā adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ na ādātabbaṃ, antamaso tiṇasalākaṃ upādāya. yo bhikkhu pādaṃ vā pādārahaṃ vā atirekapādaṃ vā adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyati, assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo. seyyathāpi nāma paṇḍupalāso bandhanā pamutto abhabbo haritatthāya, evameva bhikkhu pādaṃ vā pādārahaṃ vā atirekapādaṃ vā adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyitvā assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo. taṃ te yāvajīvaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ.
                  • "upasampannena bhikkhunā sañcicca pāṇo jīvitā na voropetabbo, antamaso kunthakipillikaṃ upādāya. yo bhikkhu sañcicca manussaviggahaṃ jīvitā voropeti, antamaso gabbhapātanaṃ upādāya, assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo. seyyathāpi nāma puthusilā dvedhā bhinnā appaṭisandhikā hoti, evameva bhikkhu sañcicca manussaviggahaṃ jīvitā voropetvā assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo. taṃ te yāvajīvaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ.
                  • upasampannena bhikkhunā uttarimanussadhammo na ullapitabbo, antamaso ‘suññāgāre abhiramāmī’ti. yo bhikkhu pāpiccho icchāpakato asantaṃ abhūtaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ ullapati jhānaṃ vā vimokkhaṃ vā samādhiṃ vā samāpattiṃ vā maggaṃ vā phalaṃ vā, assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo. seyyathāpi nāma tālo matthakacchinno abhabbo puna viruḷhiyā, evameva bhikkhu pāpiccho icchāpakato asantaṃ abhūtaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ ullapitvā assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo. taṃ te yāvajīvaṃ akaraṇīya"nti.
          • Pāḷi (conditions for being anusāsakācariya): {{7938073632568694::na, bhikkhave, bālena abyattena anusāsitabbo. yo anusāseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. anujānāmi, bhikkhave, byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena anusāsitunti.}}
          • Ordaining more than one with the same kammavācā
            • How many can ordain at the same time?→up to 3 candidates can be ordained at the same time but only under the same upajjhāya. #important
              • Pāḷi: {{0928909791386745::“Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dve tayo ekānusāvena kātuṃ, tañca kho ekena upajjhāyena, natveva nānupajjhāyena”}}
            • ...Ayaṃ ca nāgo ayaṃ ca datto āyasmato tissassa upasampadāpekkhā, parisuddhā antarāyikehi dhammehi. Paripuṇṇimesaṃ pattacīvaraṃ. Nāgo ca datto ca saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācanti.
              • Note: The verb could also be used in the singular form (yācati) since it is used in some suttas.
          • If the upajjhāya or the anusāsakācariya are pārājika is the upasampadā valid?→as long as there are at least 5 pure bhikkhus (10 within majjhimadesa) the upasampadā is valid because it is the saṅgha that ordains the candidate.
          • Hatthapāsa (kāyasamaggi) is not an issue for upasampadā because it is not mentioned. #tbc🕵 #q🙋🏼‍♂
        • abhabbapuggala
          • 13/14 abhabbapuggala for upasampadā (those who are not suited for higher ordination and ordination would not be established in them) #important
            • (11) Paṇḍakādayo... - the eleven starting with paṇḍaka
            • (1) Pārājika - one who has fallen into pārājika
            • (1) ūnavīsativasso puggalo - one who has not completed 20 years of age (from conception, 360 days per year).
              • What is the offense for ordaining a candidate who is too young and can he ordain again properly?→pācittiya for the upajjhāya. If done too soon because of miscalculation no āpatti (but ordination is not established). Candidate can ordain again properly.
              • If one has stayed in the womb for 9 months at which age can he receive high ordination?→19 years and 3 months (but according to the solar calendar of the Buddha's time an extra 5 days can be added for each year, and a day for each leap year, therefore at about 19 years old)
              • For bhī ordination wheather she was married or not affects the age of ordination: if she was married she can ordain from the age of {{5007274178897996::12}}, if not married from the age of {{5007274178897996::20.}}
              • Calculating the age of the candidate
                • At the Buddha time there were two calendars: solar calendar ({{469064526256906::360}} days a year, {{469064526256906::30}} days a month) and lunar calendar ({{469064526256906::354}} days a year). The one used for uposatha calculation is {{469064526256906::the lunar}} and for upasampadā the one used is {{469064526256906::the solar of the Buddha's time}}
                • Lunar calendar (WIP) #tbc🕵
                  • every 3 years one extra month (lacking information)
                • Present day solar calendar
                  • Leap year: every 4 years one day is added to February (29th)
                • How to calculate the age of the candidate?→To calculate the age of the candidate it is counted from conception + 5 days per year + 1 day for every 4 years (leap years) (5 days because of the difference in the solar calendar)
            • (1) bhikkhunī who disrobed
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • odātavattha→wearing lay clothes
          • sosārita: Those who are not suited for upasampadā but upasampadā would be established in them #important
            • (The same as for pabbajjā)
            • 10 ananuññato mātapitūhi dārakādi... (the ten starting with one who does not have the permission of the parents)
            • 32 hatthachinnādi (the 32 starting with the one who's hands have been cut off)
        • bhikkhus suited to become upajjhāya
          • 5 teachers and their required qualifications #important
            • pabbajjācariya: requirement: byattapaṭibala
            • upajjhāyācariya (preceptor): requirement: parisupaṭṭhāka bahussuta
            • upasampadācariya requirement: byattapaṭibala
              • yena upasampadakammavācā vuttā, ayaṃ upasampadācariyo. (upasampadācariya is the one who recited the kammavācā of the higher ordination)
            • nissayācariya (dependence teacher): requirements: parisupaṭṭhāka bahussuta
            • dhammācariya: no requirements
          • 5 qualifications for being parisupaṭṭhāka bahussuta
            • dasavassāni - Having completed ten years after higher ordination
            • Bhikkhu & Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga
            • kammākammaṁ uggahetabbaṁ- knowing how to perform vinayakammas properly
            • khandhakavattañca uggahetabbaṃ - knowing the vattakkhanda (duties) and having the ability to establish disciples in it
            • Sutta Having studied (5 options): the mahāvagga of the Dīgha Nikāya the mūlapaṇṇāsa of the Majjhima Nikāya or the first 3 chapters of the Saṃyutta Nikāya or half of the Aṅguttara Nikāya or the Dhammapada and Jātaka together with their commentaries
            • mem aid:
              • 10, 2, kamma, 14, sutta
        • after higher ordination
          • A {{6622341379521959::dukkaṭa}} transgression will result per each fall of dawn for the new bhikkhu that lives away from the preceptor. A {{6622341379521959::dukkaṭa}} transgression will result for the preceptor who confers higher ordination on bhikkhus and leave them alone. The bhikkhu that does not become a nissayamuttaka bahussuta (the learned who does not require to live under a teacher) should live with the preceptor or teacher for {{6622341379521959::all his life}}.
          • 3 bahussuta
            • ayaṃ pana bahussuto nāma tividho hoti – nissayamuccanako,
            • parisupaṭṭhāpako,
            • bhikkhunovādakoti.
          • 7 qualifications for being nissayamuttaka / nissayamuccanaka bahussuta
            • pañcavassāni - completing five years after higher ordination
            • cattāro bhāṇavārā - having memorized four bhāṇavāra of the Sutta Piṭaka
            • tisso anumodanā (maṅgala-, avamaṅgala- and bhattānumodanā) - practicing three Dhamma talks to be delivered at auspicious and non-auspicious occasions
            • dvemātikā - having memorized the two pātimokkhas
            • kathāmagga - having trained in the delivery of Dhamma sermons
            • kammākamma vinicchaya - knowing the disciplinary acts about ending uposatha, pavāraṇa and so on

          • 5 types of sampatti / vipatti (The completion of these is referred to as sampatti and the kamma is akuppa (valid). Failing to complete them is vipatti and the kamma is kuppa (invalid))
            • vatthu sampatti / vipatti - the qualities required in the upasampadāpekkha (3 for males, 4 for females)
            • ñatti sampatti / vipatti - informing the Saṅgha about the disciplinary act. It belongs to the kammoavācā of the vinayakamma. There are 5 parāmasana:
              • i. vatthu parāmasana - (vatthu refers to the candidate) The upasampadapekkha's name must be mentioned in the ñatti. Failing to do so is vatthu aparāmasana. Mentioning it as ‘ayaṃ nāgo’ is vatthu parāmasana.
                • parāmasanaṁ (nt.) √mas↔(+gen) touching (of); stroking (of); rubbing (of); caressing (of), contagion; tarnish
              • ii. saṅgha parāmasana - (saṅgha refers to the bhikkhus gathered for the disciplinary act) It should be stated as “suṇātu me, bhante saṅgho”. Failing to do so is aparāmasana. Mentioning it properly is parāmasana.
              • iii. puggala parāmasana - (puggala refers to the upajjhāya) The preceptor should be mentioned as “Nāgo tissassa upasampadāpekkho”. Failing to do so is aparāmasana. Doing it properly is parāmasana.
              • iv. ñatti parāmasana - Not stating the ñatti is ñatti aparāmasana. Stating the ñatti in the manner advised is ñatti parāmasana.
              • v. pubbe ñatti ṭhapana - ñatti should be stated prior to anusāvana (ñatti, anusāvana 1, anusāvana 2, anusāvana 3, conclusion). Not doing it in the proper order (doing anusāvana first and ñatti later) is pacchā ñatti ṭhapana (not valid). Doing it properly in order is pubbe ñatti ṭhapana.
                • ṭhapana √ṭhā (nt.)↔(+acc) fixing; fastening; setting in place; lit. causing standing
              • (mem: vatthu, saṅgha, puggala, ñatti, pubbe ñatti)
              • why the ñatti sampatti does not have ahāpana as a factor but only anusāvana has it? #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • anusāvana sampatti / vipatti - (proclamation)
              • i. vatthu parāmasana - "ayaṁ nāgo"
              • ii. saṅgha parāmasana - “suṇātu me, bhante saṅgho”
              • iii. puggala parāmasana - “Nāgo tissassa upasampadāpekkho”
              • iv. sāvaṇa ahāpana - uttering the sāvaṇa properly - Failing to do so is sāvaṇa hāpana. Uttering the anusāvana three times with correct pronunciation is sāvana ahāpana.
                • sāvaṇaṁ (nt.)↔announcement, proclamation (s.w. s)
                • hāpanaṁ (nt.)↔lessening, reduction
              • v. kāla sāvaṇa - ñatti must be done first and anusāvana after it
                • anusāvanaṁ (nt.)↔proclamation
            • sīmā sampatti / vipatti
              • The sīmā has to be properly established (sampatti). Failure to do so is vipatti.
              • two main types of sīmā

              • iii. sammukhībhūtānaṃ appaṭikkosanaṃ (the gathered bhikkhus not objecting) - If even one objects the disciplinary act will not be effective.

Tena vuccati – ‘Pārājiko hotī’ti. Tena vuccati – ‘Pārājiko hotī’ ti. Tena vuccati – ‘Pārājiko hotī’ ti. As a large rock split into two halves cannot be refixed, a monk who intentionally deprives a human being of its life cannot be a recluse or a son of the Buddha any longer. Owing to that fault, he ceases to be a recluse or a son of the Buddha.
              • uttarimanussadhammasikkhāpadaṁ Pārājiko hotīti seyyathāpi nāma tālo matthakacchinno abhabbo puna virūḷhiyā, evameva bhikkhu pāpiccho icchāpakato asantaṃ abhūtaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ ullapitvā assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo. Tena vuccati – ‘Pārājiko hotī’ ti. As a palm tree of which the top (head) is cut off does not grow any more, a monk who has falsely claimed himself to possess sublime attainments with evil desires to gain praise and gain cannot be a recluse or a son of the Buddha any longer. Owing to that fault, he ceases to be a recluse or a son of the Buddha

            • {{6646523908921242::20}} years after the enlightenment, when the Buddha was residing in {{6646523908921242::Vesālī,}} Ven. {{6646523908921242::Sudinna}} , who had the capacity to become an arahant, pressed by his mother (did what?) {{6646523908921242::he had sex with his ex-wife thrice in order to give his family an inheritor}}. The Buddha then laid down the first pārājika; he could not overcome the remorse and died as a puthujjana while his ex-wife and son ({{6646523908921242::Bījaka}}) ordained and became arahants. Later another monk was having sex with a {{6646523908921242::female monkey}}. The monk was caught, judged pārājika and the rule amended (...{{6646523908921242::antamaso tiracchānagatāyapi}}...) In the {{6646523908921242::Vajji}} Country some monks (referred to as {{6646523908921242::vajjiputtaka}}) had sex and later requested the Buddha for reordination; it was declined and the rule received a second amendment (...{{6646523908921242::bhikkhūnaṁ sikkhāsājīvasamāpanno sikkhaṁ appaccakkhāya dubbalyaṁ anāvikatvā}}...).           • background
            • while the Buddha was residing in the city of {{7653125691111182::Rājagaha}}, the King {{7653125691111182::Bimbisāra}} of Magadha issued a statement saying that {{7653125691111182::all timbre in the forests of his kingdom could be used by the monks. }} Ven. {{7653125691111182::Dhaniya}} who then had built several kuṭis for himself that had been subsequently destroyed, (did what?) {{7653125691111182::used the statement to steal timber from the king's reserves}}. The Buddha then declared the second prjk and set the value of the object of prjk to be 5 pādas or more. A group of {{7653125691111182::chabbaggiya}} bhikkhus (did what?) {{7653125691111182::stole cloth from a forest area}} and the Buddha amended the rule adding "{{7653125691111182::gāmā vā araññā vā}}" to include both village and forest.
            • attitude of a judging bhikkhu
              • a judging bhikkhu should always consider the monk as innocent until proven guilty and should try to find righteous ways his innocence is proven. If concluded as being guilty the offender should be sent to several vinaya teachers for their opinion and given a meditation subject before taking conclusions. The conclusion should be done by the offender himself.

            • "adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyeyya"

                • 5 characteristics of adinna (not given)

                  • apariccatta (not abandoned)
                  • rakkhita (protected)
                  • gopita (guarded)
                  • mamāyita (something thought of as mine)
              • stealing means {{9534292584136601::taking something that belongs to another, knowing that it does not belong to oneself, without the owner’s consent.}} The group of minds that perform this act is called {{9534292584136601::theyyasaṅkhāta}}
              • ādiyeyya is a verb that means {{42075222769019316::if taken / should take}}
            • "yathārūpe adinnādāne…tathārūpaṃ bhikkhu adinnaṃ ādiyamāno"
              • this clause refers to the value of the object of pārājika which is {{7125997933880266::one pāda or more}}
            • avaharaṇacitta (stealing mind) is→the thought of taking ownership of an object that one perceives to belong to another, not one's own, not discarded, not taking on trust or temporarily, without the consent of the owner
              • 4 situations in which the avaharaṇacitta does not arise

        • Manussaviggahasikkhāpadaṁ #edited
          • background
            • the Buddha preached the {{300041228618537::asubha meditation}} to bhikkhus who were residing in the {{300041228618537::Kūṭāgāra, in the great forests of the city of Vesālī}}and went into seclusion. After some time the bhikkhus were distressed over their own bodies and favored death. Some committed suicide, some killed each other and some approached a bearer of robes named {{300041228618537::Migalaṇḍika (mem aid: deer land)}} who ate leftovers in temples and held wrong view, and had him take their lives. The Buddha once aware of this situation declared the third pārājikā. Some of the {{300041228618537::chabbaggiya}} bhikkhus were attracted to a sick man’s wife, approached him and praised death. Having heard that the lay devotee consumed an unsuitable meal and died.             • killing animals

            • ajānantassa (using something without knowing it can cause death): such as the case of the bhikkhu who shared poisoned food with another bhikkhu not knowing it was poisoned
            • namaraṇādhippāyassa (not intending death): such as the case of an infertile woman who asked for medicine for fertility from a bhikkhu. The bhikkhu without the intention to kill gave her a medicine which resulted in her death

        • Uttarimanussadhammasikkhāpadaṁ #edited
          • background
            • the Buddha was in {{7926703886498847::Kūṭāgāra hall, Great Forest, Vesālī. }}During the rains retreat a group of bhikkhus called {{7926703886498847::Vaggumudā}} (did what?) {{7926703886498847::falsely reported each other's attainments}} during a famine in the {{7926703886498847::Vajji}} province. Coming to know of that the Buddha laid down the 4th prjk. Later some bhikkhus (did what?) {{7926703886498847::overestimated their jhāna attainments and claimed to have attained it}}. Later they realized their mistake and consulted the Buddha. He clarified that they were not guilty of a prjk and added: "{{7926703886498847::aññatra adhimānā}}" to the rule
            • notes:
              • in a few cases the background story does not match exactly the rule that developed
              • when was the first time a rule was relaxed?→when "aññātra adhimānā" was added to the 4th prjk
              • it is not suitable behavior for a monk to openly express his inabilities, past offenses and non-attainments because it weakens other's faith which may lead them to not making merits. If someone invite "arahants" to come and eat one can go happily
              • by lying about such virtues one is abusing other's faith
          • explanation of pāḷi terms
            • "yo pana bhikkhu anabhijānaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ attūpanāyikaṃ alamariyañāṇadassanaṃ samudācareyya ‘iti jānāmi, iti passāmī’ti
              • anabhijānaṃ means {{47901237649011885::knowing that one does not possess such states}}
                • why are uttarimanussadhammas called alamariyañāṇadassana?→because these pure states of wisdom are capable of eradicating defilements in the forms of suppression (vikkhambhana), eradication (samuccheda) and appeasement (paṭippassaddhi)
              • uttarimanussadhamma
                • jhāna
                • abhiññā
                  • abhiññās which are not based on jhānas, such as jātissarañāṇa or being able to see beings, are not uttarimanussadhamma
                • magga
                • phala
                • note:
                  • nibbāna is not something one can possess but expressing its attainment is included here (not for this semester)
                  • nirodhasamāpatti is not, but if one claims its attainment intending to mean one has jhāna or is an anāgāmi it is prjk
              • samudācareyya↔expresses #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • aññatra adhimānā means {{5627510970024783::except when overestimating one's attainments}}
                • noble persons do not have adhimāna
                • sotāpannas should remember clearly where they attained Nibbāna, by means of which contemplation, and so on (there are 16 things they never forget). If anāgāmi or arahant trying to scare them is a way to test them #q🙋🏼‍♂
              • attūpanāyika↔concerning oneself, applied to oneself, referring to oneself #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]

            • those beings who have attained jhānas
            • those who have attained arahatship

            • directly saying
              • listener immediately understands: prjk
              • listener does not immediately understand: tlc
            • indirectly saying
              • listener immediately understands: tlc
              • listener does not immediately understand: dkṭ
          • cases
            • knowingly making a false statement as “I have attained...I attain...I will attain...I regularly attain...I have mastered...I have fully comprehended any uttarimanussadhamma is {{5468586304619623::prjk}}
            • If with the intention of obtaining respect from others, a bhikkhu walks and behaves in a particular manner or lives in a forest monastery, a {{42833711749311454::dkṭ}} offence will be committed
            • with the desire to mention one’s superior human state, one mistakenly mentions a different superior human state instead, knowing it is a false statement, and the listener instantly understands it, it is{{4396949432250927::prjk}}
          • anāpatti
            • adhimānena (by means of overestimation)
            • anullapanādhippāyassa (not intending to boast): speaking without the intention of implying to others about the superior human states that one possesses, an offence will not be committed.
            • ummattakassa
            • khittacittassa
            • vedanaṭṭassa
            • ādikammikassa ({{9152259493068386::Vaggumudā monks}})
          • 5 sambhāra / aṅga
            • not possessing the uttarimanussadhamma one claims to have
            • claiming to have a superior human state intending to earn fame and gain
            • directly claiming it
            • the listener is human
            • the listener immediately understands
          • 5 mahācora
            • a bhikkhu who makes a group for obtaining requisites and benefits
            • a bhikkhu who implies that the sāsana was founded by himself
            • a bhikkhu who falsely accuses another of having had sex
            • a bhikkhu who gives away saṅghika requisites that cannot be distributed among individuals (avebhaṅgiya garu bhaṇḍa) such as paddy fields, gardens, furniture, steel containers etc, with the intention of pleasing the laity (without the intention to steal is a tlc, with the intention to steal it is prjk)
            • a bhikkhu who deceives the world by saying that he possesses superior human states when he actually does not possess any is the greatest thief in the word inclusive of deities

        • introduction
          • word formation
            • saṅgha ādi sesa = {{04153705918247841::group of offenses which require the assistance of the saṅgha in the beginning middle and end of the process of purification}} saṅghāt s'esa (sanskrit) = offense that makes one separated from the saṅgha

          • yāvatatiyakā↔a saṅghādisesa offence that is incurred only after a formal disciplinary act called samanubhāsanakamma is done against the offender in which the offender is admonished thrice and does not change behavior
            • what is the legal process behind a yāvatatiyakā offense?
              • misdeeds related to yāvatatiyaka offences are committed by an upasampanna
              • offender is admonished privately trice
              • the offender is brought in the presence of the Saṅgha and admonished thrice
              • samanubhāsanakamma is performed
              • if up to the end of the act the offender does not change behavior, a saṅghādisesa offence will be incurred by the offender
          • number of paṭhamāpattikā and that of yāvatatiyakā offenses
            • bhikkhus
              • 9 paṭhamāpattika
              • 4 yāvatatiyaka
            • bhikkhunīs
              • 9 paṭhamāpattika
              • 8 yāvatatiyaka
          • obs: an upasampanna who has given up on purifying himself of a saṅghādisesa offence cannot attain jhāna, magga and phala

          • background
